model_type_note: Flow Traders is a proprietary market-making firm with no client AuM and no meaningful FCF signal (reported OCF/FCF swing wildly with trading-capital working capital -- FY2025 OCF was EUR -120.6m in a profitable EUR 133.6m net-income year). This model discounts NET PROFIT (owner earnings), NOT free cash flow, at a cost of equity, analogous to a bank/insurer residual-income approach. Trading capital is treated as a required operating asset (like a bank's loan book), not excess cash, so no net-debt/net-cash bridge is applied to enterprise value -- equity value = PV(net profit stream) + PV(terminal net profit at an exit P/E).

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: 43.5m = FY2025 basic weighted-average shares (Y0 anchor for projections). 44.0m = latest actual per H1-2026 balance sheet, used as current_price context in sanity checks.
inputs.net_debt_note: No net-debt/net-cash bridge applied. FY2025 loans & borrowings EUR 164.9m (H1-2026: EUR 197.5m, $200m private credit facility + $75m revolver, both drawn to fund the Trading Capital Expansion Plan) are offset by trading capital (EUR 1,150m at H1-2026), which is REQUIRED regulatory/operating capital, not excess cash available for distribution. Interest expense on this debt (EUR 20-22m/yr projected) is already deducted inside the net-income build, so the cost of the debt is captured in the earnings stream rather than as a balance-sheet subtraction. Adding gross cash while ignoring that it collateralizes trading positions would overstate value; subtracting gross debt while ignoring the offsetting trading capital would understate it -- so both are left out of the bridge and only their P&L effect (interest expense) flows through.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Not applicable -- see model_type_note. Reported FY2025 FCF (EUR -126.9m) and OCF (EUR -120.6m) are not used anywhere in this valuation; they are working-capital artifacts of trading-capital deployment, not economic value destruction.
inputs.sbc_treatment: SBC (StockBasedComp column, EUR 17.6m FY2025 / EUR 4.4m H1-2026) is a component of 'Variable compensation paid in shares' within Employee Expenses on Flow Traders' P&L and is ALREADY fully expensed within reported Net Income (confirmed via FY2022 Annual Report Note 12: 'Total expenses arising from equity settled share-based payments EUR 33.253m' sits inside Employee Expenses feeding EBIT, and the cash flow statement adds it back as a non-cash item to reconcile Net Profit to Operating Cash Flow). Therefore NO additional earnings deduction for SBC is applied (doing so would double-count the cost). The only remaining adjustment is DILUTION: net share count growth from vesting less any buybacks/treasury absorption.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2022 Annual Report Note 12 (Employee Expenses / Share Based Payments); StockBasedComp column in FLOW.AS_Metrics.csv cross-checked against combined equity-settled + cash-settled SBP totals.
inputs.dilution_note: Shares outstanding: FY2024 43.1m -> FY2025 43.5m -> H1-2026 44.0m, i.e. net dilution of roughly 1.0%/yr even after the small FY2024 buyback (EUR 11.8m) and zero FY2025 buyback. No dividend or buyback is planned through at least 2030 per Horizon 2030 guidance (capital fully retained/reinvested), so this modest ~1.0%/yr net dilution rate is projected flat across all scenarios and all years.

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: FCF CAGRs omitted -- FCF is not a meaningful metric for a market maker (see model_type_note). SBC-adjusted FCF is not applicable since SBC is already inside net income, not an add-back to a cash flow base.
historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: 3-year equity/book-value CAGR (FY2022->FY2025, +12.7%) is the primary conservative anchor per the standard growth-rate selection hierarchy, though it is not used directly to drive the NTI projection (which is instead built bottom-up off a mid-cycle NTI base with structural ETF-market growth assumptions, per company-specific modeling guidance). The 5-year NTI, EPS and FCF CAGRs are deeply negative purely because FY2020 (NTI EUR 933m) was an anomalous COVID-volatility peak used as the start-year comparator; this is a base-effect artifact, not a business decline. The pre-COVID-base 6-year NTI CAGR (FY2019->FY2025) of 14.4% and net-income CAGR of 16.6% corroborate that mid-teens NTI growth is achievable in strong-volatility regimes, and this magnitude anchors the bull-case growth assumptions.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 5-year NTI/EPS CAGRs (-12% / -21%) diverge by more than 30pp from the 5-year equity CAGR (+8.0%) and from the 3-year equity CAGR (+12.7%). This is entirely a FY2020 COVID-base distortion (NTI EUR 933m vs. EUR 300-486m normal years), not a structural divergence, and does not indicate deteriorating fundamentals -- equity/book value has compounded steadily even through the FY2023 volatility trough.
historical_growth.notes: Because owner earnings equal reported net income (no SBC deduction, see sbc_treatment), there is no gap between a 'reported' and 'adjusted' earnings CAGR series for this company -- the SBC-growing-faster-than-cash-flow concern flagged for buyback-light/high-SBC names does not apply here since SBC is a real P&L expense already embedded in the historical net income series used above.

base.description: Structural ETF/ETP market growth (approx. 12%/yr per PwC 'ETFs 2030' forecast) partially captured by Flow Traders (NTI grows 6.0-7.0%/yr, below market growth to reflect competitive share pressure from Citadel Securities/Jane Street and incomplete monetization of APAC volume growth). EBITDA margin recovers gradually from FY2025's 41.4% toward 42% by Y5 -- well short of the Horizon 2030 >45% ambition, which is treated as bull-case territory. Fixed opex starts at the FY2026 guidance midpoint (EUR 240m, vs. EUR 235-245m guided range) and grows ~6%/yr thereafter (operating leverage: opex grows slower than NTI). Interest expense reflects the fully-drawn $200m private credit facility + $75m revolver (EUR 20-22m/yr, consistent with the H1 2026 annualized run-rate of ~EUR 19.6m). D&A grows with continued technology/AI investment. Effective tax rate normalizes toward 21% (Dutch/multi-jurisdictional blended rate).
base.coe_rationale: 12% cost of equity reflects: risk-free rate ~3.3% (German 10yr Bund, mid-2026), equity risk premium ~5.5%, beta materially above 1 (~1.4-1.5) for a highly volatility-dependent earnings stream with no revenue floor, plus a small/mid-cap Euronext Amsterdam illiquidity premium. This sits at the upper end of typical financials CoE to compensate for structural earnings cyclicality (NTI can move 30-50%+ QoQ) and rising financial leverage from the new credit facilities.

bull.description: Horizon-2030-consistent trajectory: elevated/sustained volatility regime, full deployment of the expanded trading-capital base (record EUR 1,150m and growing), APAC and traditional-business acceleration continue at 1H26 rates, EBITDA margin reaches and holds the >45% Horizon 2030 ambition by Y4-Y5. NTI grows from EUR 485.8m to EUR 935m by Y5 (essentially in line with, though just short of, the >EUR 1bn 2030 NTI target, appropriately since Y5 in this model = FY2030). Fixed opex still grows (funding the growth ambition) but interest expense declines as facilities amortize/earnings outgrow the fixed debt cost.
bull.coe_rationale: 11% CoE in the bull case reflects modestly reduced perceived cyclical risk as Horizon 2030 execution (six strategic pillars, record trading capital, >45% EBITDA margin) demonstrates durable structural earnings power beyond pure volatility-timing.

bear.description: Prolonged low-volatility 'volatility drought' resembling FY2023 (NTI EUR 300.3m, EBITDA margin 22.2%, net margin 12.1%) and the muted conditions flagged in the 2Q26 pre-close call (VIX down to 18.3 from 20.3, market ETF value traded -14% QoQ). NTI contracts in Y1-Y2 before stabilizing at a depressed plateau. Fixed opex remains sticky even in the downturn (technology/AI hiring commitments already made, per FY2026 guidance creep from EUR 220-230m to EUR 235-245m). Interest expense stays elevated (facility fully drawn, slow deleveraging without earnings growth) before easing modestly late in the horizon. Competitive pressure from Citadel Securities/Jane Street intensifies and digital-assets/crypto stays depressed.
bear.coe_rationale: 14% CoE in the bear case reflects materialized cyclical risk, a sustained low-volatility regime with no earnings floor, elevated leverage concern relative to a shrunken earnings base, and the kind of investor risk-aversion toward volatile-earnings financials seen historically when Flow Traders traded at single-digit P/E multiples (e.g., FY2023).

entry_price.methodology: Price at which buying today, collecting the base-case projected NET INCOME (as the distributable-earnings analog to FCF) over 5 years and exiting at the base-case terminal value in Year 5 earns a 15% IRR. Interim net income is discounted at 15% (not COE); the terminal value itself is still computed using COE-based Gordon growth / exit-P/E-cap logic (the fair price a buyer pays at exit), only the discounting back to today uses the 15% hurdle. No net-debt adjustment is applied, consistent with the equity-value bridge used throughout (see net_debt_note).

base.note: At EUR 26.48, the stock trades approximately 19% below the base-case 15%-IRR entry price of EUR 32.75, i.e. buying today at the base case would be expected to exceed a 15% annualized return to fair value, consistent with the entry price sitting sensibly below (not far below) intrinsic value of EUR 36.68 given base NTI growth (~6.5% avg) is below the 15% hurdle.

bull.pv_terminal_at_hurdle_note: recomputed at 15% discounting of the COE-based bull terminal value

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = cost of equity 8% to 16% (top to bottom), holding base-case NTI/margin/opex assumptions and the 11x exit-P/E terminal cap constant. Columns = terminal growth 1.5% to 3.5% (left to right). At low discount rates (8-10%), the 11x exit-P/E cap binds regardless of terminal growth (Gordon growth would otherwise imply an unrealistically rich exit multiple), which is why those rows are flat across columns -- this is the cap doing its job, not a modeling error. Current price of EUR 26.48 sits near the 14-16% discount-rate rows, implying the market is pricing Flow Traders' cost of equity well above this model's 12% base-case assumption -- consistent with the stock's persistent single-digit-to-low-teens historical P/E and investor skepticism about earnings durability.

probability_weighted.rationale: Base 50%: most likely outcome reflecting continued moderate-volatility market conditions, structural ETF-market growth partially captured by Flow Traders, and gradual margin recovery well short of the Horizon 2030 >45% EBITDA-margin ambition. Bull 25%: Horizon 2030 execution broadly on track -- sustained elevated volatility, full trading-capital deployment, APAC/traditional acceleration continuing at 1H26 rates. Bear 25%: a prolonged FY2023-style volatility drought materializes (a fully plausible near-term outcome given 2Q26 already showed sequential deceleration from 1Q26), compounded by the now-higher fixed-cost and interest-expense base.
probability_weighted.weighted_iv_note: 35.74 is the REBUILT weighted IV adopted as the headline on 2026-08-28 (bear 12.38 x 0.25 + base 36.02 x 0.50 + bull 58.54 x 0.25). The as-published 38.29 is retained in weighted_iv_as_published; it was reached through three input errors (declining variable-comp share, stale NTI base, over-severe bear) and sits at the extreme top of the defensible EUR 30-40 range, central ~34. See corrections_2026_08_28.
probability_weighted.upside_note: 26.6% is the rebuilt weighted IV 35.74 against current_price 28.24. The as-published 44.6% belonged to the superseded 38.29 and was left behind when the headline was rebuilt on 2026-08-28; it is retained in upside_from_current_pct_as_published.

sanity_check.basis_note: P/E and EV/EBITDA on SBC-adjusted earnings both sides (NetIncome-SBC, EBITDA-SBC) per repo convention; will NOT match published GAAP multiples. Note SBC is already expensed in Flow Traders GAAP net income, so this adjusted basis is doubly conservative but consistent across implied vs historical.

historical_averages_ex_outliers.outliers_excluded: FY2020 (COVID volatility-spike peak earnings). FY2019/FY2023 trough-earnings years inflate the P/E average (44.2x in FY2023 is denominator collapse, not a real rating) - the ex-trough P/E average is also shown.

dcf_agent_qualitative_check.historical_pe_range_ex_covid: 5x-12x (FY2023 trough ~5.6x on annualized H1; FY2018 peak ~13x)
dcf_agent_qualitative_check.verdict: Base intrinsic value of EUR 36.68 implies roughly 12.0x FY2025 EPS and 9.2x terminal-year (FY2030E) EPS -- both within or below the historical 5-12x ex-COVID trading range and below the exit-P/E cap of 11x used for the terminal value itself (the model's 9.2x actual outcome sits below its own 11x ceiling because the discount factor and Gordon-vs-cap comparison bind at a lower effective multiple once discounted). This is a conservative, not aggressive, valuation relative to Flow Traders' own trading history and to Virtu Financial's 12-14x. The bear case (EUR 12.34, -53.4%) provides a credible downside anchor consistent with a repeat of FY2023 conditions (net margin 12.1% actual vs. bear-case Y1 net margin 12.5% assumed).
dcf_agent_qualitative_check.peak_earnings_check: H1-2026 net income annualized (x2) = EUR 182.4m vs. base-case Y5 (FY2030E) net income of EUR 182.4m -- i.e. the model's FIVE-YEAR-OUT base case merely matches, not exceeds, the CURRENT annualized run-rate, despite assuming positive structural NTI growth. This is intentionally conservative: it implicitly assumes margin/cost normalization (rising fixed opex, higher interest expense, no assumption that 1H26's above-trend traditional-business growth persists) roughly offsets NTI growth over the projection window, rather than compounding H1-2026 momentum forward. The bull case, by contrast, explicitly extrapolates Horizon 2030 execution (NTI approaching EUR 935m by Y5, just under the >EUR 1bn 2030 target).
dcf_agent_qualitative_check.warning_banner: Flow Traders' earnings are structurally cyclical (single-quarter swings of 30-50%+ tied to market volatility/VIX) with NO recurring revenue base. All scenario outputs should be treated as mid-cycle fair-value estimates, not near-term price targets. The stock may reasonably trade at or below the bear-case IV (EUR 12.34) for extended periods during low-volatility regimes, as it did through FY2023.

valuation_context.commentary: CORRECTED 2026-08-28. The prior commentary stated 'the probability-weighted intrinsic value of approximately EUR 27-28 implies the stock is roughly fairly valued to modestly undervalued'. That figure is NOT the model's probability-weighted IV, which is EUR 38.29 (bear 12.34 x 0.25 + base 36.68 x 0.50 + bull 67.48 x 0.25). EUR 27-28 corresponds to the 14-16% cost-of-equity rows of the sensitivity matrix, i.e. the model's value at a materially higher discount rate than the 12% base case. The two numbers were reported in the same file without reconciliation, and the dashboard renders the 38.29 figure as the headline 'Prob-Weighted IV'. || SEPARATELY, the EUR 38.29 headline should be treated with caution pending the 2026-08-28 deep dive: an external template (Sven Carlin Research Platform, Sept-2025, FLOW tab) independently produces EUR 39.83 for this name, but does so by (a) zeroing the dividend payout so that 100% of value is a terminal P/E on 2034 EPS, (b) assuming 5-15%/yr EPS growth in ALL scenarios including the worst case, against a realised FY2015-FY2025 EPS CAGR of +3.9% and FY2018-FY2025 of -1.7%, and (c) applying 15x/20x/10x exit multiples versus a current 8.6x and peer Virtu at 12-14x. Re-running that same template with realised growth and this model's own exit multiples yields ~EUR 17.8. The convergence of EUR 38.29 and EUR 39.83 is therefore NOT independent corroboration.
valuation_context.commentary_prior_2026_08_01: At EUR 26.48, Flow Traders trades at 8.6x FY2025 earnings and 1.20x H1-2026 book value -- a persistent discount versus U.S. peer Virtu Financial (approx. 12-14x earnings), reflecting the market's structural skepticism about the durability/predictability of NTI. The probability-weighted intrinsic value of approximately EUR 27-28 implies the stock is roughly fairly valued to modestly undervalued at mid-cycle assumptions, while the base-case entry price (EUR 32.75, the price that would earn a 15% IRR to fair value) sits meaningfully above the current price, suggesting a reasonable margin of safety if base-case assumptions hold. Key overhangs suppressing the multiple: (1) extreme quarter-to-quarter earnings cyclicality tied to VIX/volatility, most recently visible in the 2Q26 sequential deceleration (NTI -5% QoQ, net profit -19% QoQ) after a strong 1Q26; (2) dividend and buyback both suspended through at least 2030 under Horizon 2030 capital retention policy, removing a historical valuation support; (3) EUR 197.5m net debt (H1-2026) and a rapidly rising interest-expense run-rate (~EUR 20m annualized, from near-zero in H1-2025) now layered onto an already-cyclical earnings stream; (4) fixed-opex guidance raised twice within two months in 2026 (EUR 220-230m to EUR 235-245m), raising the NTI level required to sustain the Horizon 2030 >45% EBITDA-margin target. A re-rating catalyst would likely require either sustained elevated volatility validating the >EUR 1bn Horizon 2030 NTI ambition, demonstrated return on the expanded trading-capital base, or eventual dividend resumption.

headline_iv_caveat_2026_08_28.bear_grounding: Bear assumes a 24.0% Y1 EBITDA margin. FY2023 ACTUAL was 22.5%. The bear case is historically grounded, not pessimistic. 10yr realised EBITDA margin range 22.5%-62.9%.
headline_iv_caveat_2026_08_28.terminal_value_share: 60.8% (bear) / 66.6% (base) / 74.0% (bull) of value is terminal, on a business whose earnings are a function of market volatility and are not forecastable one year ahead.
headline_iv_caveat_2026_08_28.status: Headline IV under review pending deep dive commissioned 2026-08-28.

valuation_philosophy: Flow Traders is a proprietary trading firm / electronic market maker with NO recurring revenue, NO client AuM, and reported cash flow figures that are economically meaningless for valuation (FY2025 OCF of EUR -120.6m in a EUR 133.6m net-income year, driven entirely by trading-capital working-capital swings). This model therefore discounts projected NET PROFIT (owner earnings) at a cost of equity, in the spirit of a bank/insurer residual-income framework, rather than a traditional FCF DCF. Three disciplined constraints govern the build: (1) SBC is confirmed already-expensed within reported net income (FY2022 Annual Report Note 12), so it is NOT deducted a second time -- only the resulting ~1.0%/yr net share dilution (vesting less minimal/absent buybacks) is modeled, consistent with the 'no dividend/buyback through at least 2030' guidance; (2) the NTI base is FY2025's actual EUR 485.8m -- a genuine mid-cycle year (above the EUR 114m FY2021-2025 raw net-income average but conspicuously NOT extrapolating the stronger Q1-2026/H1-2026 run-rate, since 2Q26 already showed sequential deceleration versus 1Q26), with margins, fixed opex (FY2026 guidance EUR 235-245m) and interest expense (annualizing toward ~EUR 20m) built up from components rather than held flat; (3) terminal value is capped at a conservative exit P/E (11x base, 13x bull, 9x bear) whenever Gordon growth would imply a richer multiple, preventing a small change in terminal growth from swinging the valuation on an inherently cyclical earnings stream. Trading capital is treated as a required operating asset (not distributable excess cash), so no net-debt bridge is applied to equity value; the cost of the associated debt is captured instead through the interest-expense line inside net income. Investors should treat the base intrinsic value of EUR 36.68 as a mid-cycle fair-value estimate, not a near-term price target, and should expect the stock to trade at or below the bear-case IV (EUR 12.34) for extended stretches during low-volatility regimes, exactly as it did through FY2023.

corrections_2026_08_28.summary: Two offsetting errors found in the published model. Headline weighted IV 38.29 is roughly the right neighbourhood but reached by cancelling errors, and the scenario spread is not credible.

error_1_variable_opex_share.issue: projections.base.implied_variable_opex falls from 25.7% to 22.9% of gross profit (NTI less fixed opex) across the projection. Variable compensation is contractual and does not shrink.
error_1_variable_opex_share.evidence: FY2025 AR: firm-wide variable remuneration pool EUR74.4m, 'corresponding to 32.5% of the operating result in 2025'. Empirically, variable opex / gross profit by year: FY2021 28.8%, FY2022 38.2%, FY2023 46.5%, FY2024 24.8%, FY2025 29.4%. Mean 33.6%. The model's 22.9-25.7% is BELOW every observed year.
error_1_variable_opex_share.note: The 32.5% headline applies to a 'operating result' base that differs from gross profit; the correct empirical ratio to hold flat is ~29.4% (FY2025) to 33.6% (5yr mean).
error_1_variable_opex_share.effect: Holding the share flat at 29.4% and changing nothing else: base IV 36.68 -> 33.22. At the 33.6% five-year mean: 30.77.

error_2_stale_nti_base.issue: Base case anchors FY2026E NTI at 519.8 (FY2025 485.8 grown 7%). H1-2026 actual NTI was 303.7, annualising to 607.4 -- the model is ~14% BELOW the current-year run rate. Its FY2026E net income of 134.7 is exceeded by H1-2026 alone (91.2 in six months).
error_2_stale_nti_base.effect: Understates the earnings base, offsetting error 1 in the opposite direction.

error_3_bear_case_too_severe.issue: Bear IV 12.34 implies ~0.56x book against largely liquid trading assets, and assumes the variable-compensation absorber does not work.
error_3_bear_case_too_severe.evidence: FY2023 demonstrated the absorber: variable employee expense fell 44% while NTI fell 35%. Re-running an FY2023 NTI repeat (300.3) against the FY2026 cost base still yields positive net income (~EUR5m, EPS ~0.12). Breakeven requires NTI below ~280, not seen since FY2019 on a capital base one third the size.
error_3_bear_case_too_severe.effect: The company is very unlikely to be loss-making in a drought. The realistic bear is near-zero EPS with multiple compression, not insolvency.

rebuilt_valuation.method: FY2026 run-rate NTI base (607), variable share held flat at 29.4%, fixed opex per guidance, D&A/interest/tax paths unchanged, shares +1%/yr.
rebuilt_valuation.cross_checks: Independent deep dive (2026-08-28) put normalized through-cycle EPS at EUR3.50-3.90 and fair value at EUR30-40, central ~34. Justified P/B on 17.4% normalized ROE gives EUR31.84 (CoE 13%) to EUR39.80 (CoE 11%). Corrected-DCF, normalized-earnings and justified-P/B methods agree on a EUR30-40 range.

fair_value_conclusion.vs_price_29_06: +17% to central, not the +32% the published 38.29 implied.
fair_value_conclusion.verdict: 38.29 is at the extreme top of the defensible range and should not be used as the headline IV.

price_history_2026_08_28.pb_floor_note: The 0.87x trough in 2024 occurred in a GOOD earnings year (FY2024 EPS 3.70) -- the multiple compressed on sentiment and capital-raise concerns alone, not a drought. A trough multiple coinciding with drought EPS is the genuine tail risk and has not been observed. Today's 1.32x sits at the TOP of the post-2022 range. On H1-2026 BVPS of 22.05, a repeat of the 2024 trough multiple implies EUR19.18, i.e. -34%.
price_history_2026_08_28.structural_note: The P/B de-rating from 4.66x (2016) to ~1.3x is structural, not sentiment: trading capital roughly doubled (EUR584m -> EUR1,150m), so the business became far more balance-sheet-intensive. A capital-heavy market maker earns a lower multiple of book.
